scenes.title: Duck Under the Fringe
scenes.summary: Outside at the street gate, M2 ties his four-metre cloth banner across the stone arch, hanging down to knee height with an enormous two-metre teapot emblem.
scenes.intro: At nine-thirty Thursday morning on {STREET}, {M2} climbs down two steps of the wooden ladder and spreads his arms proudly before a giant cream canvas wall blocking the entire gate of {SHOW}, while {F1} and {M1} stare from the pavement. Listen first.
story: M2
Stand across the cobbles and drink in the grandeur, {F1} and {M1}!
F1
Everyone on {STREET} can definitely see that giant gold teapot from three blocks away!
M1
Quick question, boss: how does a paying guest actually walk INTO {SHOW} now?
M2
Simply part the lower gold fringe politely and bend slightly at the waist!
F1
Bend slightly?! {M1} would have to crawl on hands and knees like a badger!
M1
Try carrying two suitcases under knee-high canvas and tell me how five-star that feels.
M2
Wait—why is that painted gold teapot in the middle taller than {F2}?!
F1
Because you ticked Giant Emblem Box Nine without pulling your glasses down, {M2}!
M1
Hold on—feel that first fat drop of warm rain hitting my cap brim?
F1
Oh no, that passing Thursday sun-shower just reached {STREET}!
M2
Save the gold fringe! Untie the left rope before the border ribbon gets soaked!
M1
Left knot loose, right knot loose—fold inward toward the middle on three!
scenes.outro: A two-metre gold teapot and a sudden sun-shower bring the giant gate curtain down in record time! See you inside next time.

scenes.title: Scissors and Pennant Flags
scenes.summary: Spreading the dry canvas banner across Room 9, F3 and F1 show a gloomy M2 how to cut its clean cream-and-gold borders into cheerful festival pennant flags.
scenes.intro: Inside bright Room 9 while the brief sun-shower passes outside, {M2} sits sighing beside the folded four-metre canvas until {F3} arrives carrying her sewing basket alongside {F1}. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
Four metres of expensive washable canvas, and it blocked my own front gate.
F3
Cheer up, {M2}; good heavy cream cotton never goes to waste around a sewing basket!
F1
Wait—what are you measuring along the gold-trimmed border with your ribbon tape, {F3}?
F3
Twenty neat triangles, each thirty centimetres wide, sewn along a braided white cord!
F1
FESTIVAL PENNANT BUNTING! High across the arch where tall guests walk underneath freely!
M2
Hold on—cream and gold triangular flags fluttering above the gate like a royal regatta?!
F3
And we cut out a clean square around the gold teapot emblem for {F2}!
F1
Plus two long cream table runners left over for the outdoor pastry tables!
M2
{F3}, {F1}—you mean my four-metre mistake actually bought THREE matching festival decorations?!
F3
Thread two needles and hand {M2} the fabric shears so he earns the credit!
F1
Cut straight along my pencil line, boss—with your glasses ON your nose!
M2
Glasses firmly on my nose—watch the finest tailor on {STREET} go to work!
scenes.outro: Sharp shears and {F3}'s clever eye turn one giant gate blocker into twenty pennant flags, two runners, and a café sign! See you next time.

scenes.title: Four Cedar Screens in Place
scenes.summary: After the cobblestones dry in the afternoon sun, M3 and M4 stand all four linen-wrapped cedar acoustic screens along the brick arcade while F2 adds pots of fresh rosemary.
scenes.intro: By two in the afternoon, golden sun dries the courtyard stones. {M3} and {M4} carry out four tall oatmeal-linen cedar screens along the brick arcade while {F2} follows with terracotta pots of green rosemary. Listen first.
story: M4
Set screen number four beside the stone arch—check those oak feet on the flagstones!
M3
Steady as a tree trunk, {M4}, without touching one centimetre of historic brick.
F2
Step back and look: the warm oatmeal linen matches our cream tablecloths beautifully!
M4
Where do you want these four terracotta pots of rosemary and thyme, Chef?
F2
Tuck one pot beside each wooden base so every breeze smells like a garden kitchen!
M3
Now comes the real scientific test: let us make noisy festival chatter together!
F2
Count me in! Two mint teas, four honey twists, lovely weather today on {STREET}!
M4
Clinking spoons against saucers right beside the fountain—how does the echo sound, {M3}?
M3
Gone! All that sharp brick slap vanished right into the double linen weave!
F2
Call {F3} inside Room Nine to play a scale while {F1} listens at the gate!
M4
If soft piano notes carry past fifty clinking teacups, little brother, you are a wizard!
M3
Green shutters wide open—ready inside Room Nine whenever you are, {F3}!
scenes.outro: Oatmeal linen, warm cedar, and fragrant rosemary quiet the brick echo right on cue for the music test! See you next time.

scenes.title: Crystal Clear at the Gate
scenes.summary: Standing out by the street gate arch while F3 plays inside Room 9, F1 reports back to M3 and F3 that every soft note floats clearly onto {STREET}.
scenes.intro: {F3} plays a sparkling passage on the walnut piano inside Room 9, then steps out to the sunroom doorway as {F1} hurries back from the front gate arch toward {M3}. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F1
{F3}! {M3}! Come see who stopped outside on the pavement just now!
F3
Did the piano carry all the way through the stone archway onto {STREET}, {F1}?
F1
Every single grace note floated out the gate like a bird on a breeze!
M3
Zero muddiness around the high register near the fountain basin?
F1
Clear as bell glass—three shoppers with market baskets stopped outside and applauded!
F3
{M3}, your four cedar screens turned this stone courtyard into a true chamber hall!
M3
Teamwork between Grandfather and his saw, {M4} and his joints, and good heavy linen.
F1
And wait until you see {F2} hanging the cut-out gold teapot sign behind her counter!
F3
I just finished stitching the twentieth cream-and-gold triangle onto our pennant cord too.
M3
So music is ready, pastries are ready, and the plaque goes up tomorrow afternoon!
F1
Let us help {F2} dress the café booth before the Thursday evening mail arrives!
F3
Lead the way, {F1}—this courtyard already feels like Saturday morning!
scenes.outro: Shoppers on {STREET} applaud through the open gate, proving the courtyard acoustics are festival-ready! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Gold Teapot Booth
scenes.summary: At the café corner, F2 and F1 unveil the rescued gold teapot emblem and crisp cream runners, restoring M2's pride in his accidental banner order.
scenes.intro: At four-thirty at the courtyard café counter, {F2} and {F1} smooth two crisp cream canvas runners with gold trim across the serving tables just as {M2} walks out carrying a teacup. Listen first.
story: F2
Close your eyes for three seconds, boss... one, two, three—now look at my counter!
M2
Great heavens! My giant gold teapot looks like a custom-painted bakery crest on that wall!
F1
And look down at the two serving tables: matching cream canvas runners with gold borders!
F2
Thick washable cotton, crumb-proof, wind-heavy, and bright enough to spot from the gate!
M2
Did I not tell everyone at eight this morning that bold canvas projects confidence?!
F1
With minor surgical assistance from {F3} and a pair of sharp fabric shears, {M2}!
F2
Set your three-tier brass pastry stand right in the centre of runner number one, boss.
M2
Look how the brass tiers catch the gold trim—Clock-Square Courtyard has nothing like this!
F1
And {M1} is outside on the ladder right now hanging {F3} and your pennant flags!
M2
I must go supervise the angle from the pavement immediately—with my glasses down!
F2
Go admire your flags, {M2}, while {F1} checks the evening festival post!
F1
Look, a thick bundle of printed festival booklets just landed in the gate box!
scenes.outro: The café booth gleams in cream and gold while {M1} climbs the gate ladder—and a fresh bundle of festival booklets arrives! See you next time.

scenes.title: Stringing the Pennant Arch
scenes.summary: Outside at the street gate, M1 fastens the twenty cream-and-gold pennant flags high across the stone arch while F3 checks the curve from below.
scenes.intro: In warm late-afternoon light on {STREET}, {M1} stands near the top of his wooden ladder fastening braided white cord above the keystone while {F3} watches from the opposite kerb. Let us listen in first.
story: F3
Two centimetres higher on the right hook, {M1}... stop right there, that curve is lovely!
M1
Three full metres above the threshold—even a tall basketball player walks under cleanly.
F3
Watch the twenty cream-and-gold triangles flutter gently without blocking the carved stone arch.
M1
You sew straighter seams in an hour than any express factory in {CITY}, madam.
F3
Thirty years of teaching piano scales teaches a person steady rhythm with a needle too!
M1
Tomorrow afternoon I bolt the polished oval brass plaque right below the left lantern.
F3
Have you enjoyed seeing the old guesthouse come alive with neighbours these past weeks, {M1}?
M1
More footsteps to sweep on Sunday morning, madam—though the music is first-rate.
F3
Coming from you, {M1}, that practically counts as a standing ovation!
M1
Hold the ladder steady while I climb down—why is {F1} waving a booklet?
F3
She looks rather surprised—let us step inside the lobby and see what happened!
M1
Whenever City Hall prints a schedule, I reach for my carpenter pencil.
scenes.outro: Twenty cream-and-gold pennants dance high above the gate, just as {F1} waves the newly printed festival booklet from the lobby! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Printed Festival Booklet
scenes.summary: Opening the official Festival Guidebook at the front desk, F1, M2, and M3 discover {SHOW}'s featured concert and tasting slot was printed for ten Saturday morning instead of four in the afternoon!
scenes.intro: Inside at the front desk, {F1} lays open page six of the newly delivered {CITY} Historic Courtyard Festival Guidebook before {M2} and {M3}. Listen first.
story: M2
Read our write-up aloud, {F1}! Did they spell {SHOW} and {STREET} properly?!
F1
Every name is spelled right, {M2}, yet look closely at the bold clock time above!
M3
Featured Opening Concert and Pastry Showcase at {SHOW}: Saturday Morning at TEN SHARP?!
M2
TEN IN THE MORNING?! We requested four in the afternoon—Clock-Square opens at ten!
F1
Look at page two: Clock-Square Courtyard AND {SHOW} are listed opposite each other at ten!
M3
Wait—that means {F2} has to bake sixty honey-fig twists at dawn on Saturday!
M2
Worse! Half the festival crowd goes to three-time champion Clock-Square at ten sharp!
F1
Hold on, {M2}—why is {M4} jogging through our front gate waving his jacket?!
M3
My brother never runs unless something big happened across the square at City Hall!
M2
Did the committee cancel Saturday?! Did another courier bring a five-metre banner?!
F1
Catch your breath at the counter, {M4}—we just saw the ten-sharp morning time!
M3
Come into the café corner with {F2} so {M4} tells everyone at once!
scenes.outro: Ten sharp Saturday morning replaces four in the afternoon—and {M4} has just sprinted in with even bigger news from Clock Square! Final scene of Episode 4!

scenes.title: Trouble Up at Clock Square
scenes.summary: In the café corner, M4 reports that an old street water main burst outside Clock-Square Courtyard, stranding their Saturday morning musicians and craft tables without a dry courtyard.
scenes.intro: Gathering quickly around the café counter, {F1} and {F2} pour {M4} a glass of cool water as he delivers urgent Thursday evening news from across {STREET}. Listen first.
story: M4
Twenty minutes ago, an old cast-iron water pipe burst right up by Clock Square!
F2
Oh no! Was anybody hurt, {M4}? Did water reach the houses?!
M4
Everyone is safe and dry, yet repair crews dug up their entire front entrance!
F1
Wait—you mean Clock-Square Courtyard has to keep its front gates closed until Monday?!
M4
Closed all weekend! That is why the printer moved {SHOW} into the ten-sharp opening slot!
F2
Poor neighbours! What happens to their woodcarver and their two young flute players?!
M4
They stood on the pavement holding their flute cases looking completely heartbroken.
F1
Hold everything, {F2}—we have a sunny east brick arcade AND four acoustic screens!
F2
Are you thinking the exact same thing I am thinking right now, {F1}?!
M4
Wait—invite your three-time rival courtyard to share {SHOW} on Saturday morning?!
F1
Let us ask {M2} right now—what good is an open gate with neighbours outside?!
F2
Put on a fresh pot of tea; Friday is about to get twice as exciting!
scenes.outro: A burst street pipe closes the three-time champion's gate—and sparks a generous idea that will test {M2}'s festival heart! End of Episode 4—see you in Episode 5!
